transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, it's nice to meet you too. Well, I made the appointment because I just feel like I’m always up and moving around. Even on what is supposed to be a quiet day at home, I end up bouncing from sorting out the garden club list, over to my knitting bag, and then to looking through some travel papers... usually before I’ve really finished any one of those things. I just can't seem to settle down, so I thought I should finally come in and talk to someone about it.
When you’re feeling especially up and busy like this, do you need much less sleep than usual?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still sleep about the same amount I always have. I mean, I might have a little trouble winding down right at bedtime because my mind is still going, but I don't feel like I can just skip sleep or anything. I still need my seven or eight hours to feel right the next day.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still and finishing things when you were a child?

Yes, I did. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was bright but scattered. I was always losing my papers, talking out of turn, and just wiggling in my seat before I'd even finished my work. It's really been a lifelong thing.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different everyday things?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things now and then, like anyone my age... maybe hoping my pension check comes on time or wondering if my grandkids are doing alright. But I wouldn't say I spend a lot of time worrying about everything. It's more just... I can't seem to stop moving and doing things, rather than sitting around feeling anxious or worried.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?

No, not really. I mean, I usually know what I'm going to say before I open my mouth. I might be always on the go, but I don't just blurt things out or jump into a situation without thinking it over first. I'd say I'm pretty careful about that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern beginning in childhood of hyperactivity/restlessness and distractibility with difficulty finishing tasks, supported by childhood teacher reports of being scattered, losing papers, talking out of turn, and constant seat-wiggling. Current symptoms include being constantly on the go, shifting between tasks without completion, and inability to settle down. Mania is less likely because there is no decreased need for sleep, and generalized anxiety is less likely because excessive pervasive worry is denied. Although impulsivity is not strongly endorsed, the presentation is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive type / hyperkinetic disorder.
